chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The son of the son stands in the place of the father."

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar wrote to Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him): A man died and left behind the daughter of his daughter, and his brother from his father and mother. Who should inherit? He (peace be upon him) wrote: "In that case, the inheritance is for the nearest, if God wills."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: As for what some of our companions mentioned, that the offspring of the offspring do not inherit with the parents, and their argument for that was the report of Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, in his saying: "The son of the son stands in the place of the son if the deceased has no offspring and no other heir." He said: "And no other heir" — they are the two parents, nothing else — so it is an error.

Because his saying (peace be upon him) "and no other heir" means that if the deceased does not have the son through whom the son of the son approaches, or the daughter through whom the daughter of the daughter approaches, and there is no other heir for him among the offspring of the loins other than the two parents.
And that which clarifies what we mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.يَقُومُ مَقَامَ: Stands in the place of / represents

ai.seo_question: Does the father exclude the grandson from inheritance in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the Shia position that a grandson (ibn al-ibn) inherits alongside the father, refuting the view that the father's presence excludes him. He interprets the phrase 'no other heir' in related reports as referring specifically to the absence of direct offspring (son or daughter) through whom the grandson approaches, rather than a general exclusion by the father. This distinction highlights the Shia principle of proximity in inheritance, where the grandson's right is derived through his father, allowing co-inheritance with the paternal line.
